# T0.19 — packaging v8 (suite tsvc_c4: the contrast set's loops and s341 on data that move) on the server, before a model reads it

*Generated by `agent/tools/campaign.py reports` from `results/campaign.json` and the experiment record (`agent/THESIS_EXPERIMENTS.md`). Edit those, then regenerate — not this file.*

**Status:** running

## The question

Are the nine tsvc_c4 packages sound to measure on — built alike on both machines, at a measurable size, each reference verified and faster — which of the eight new loops does DiscoPoP alone parallelize (the control) and which does it leave unchanged (the set under test), and is s341 on its new data the loop DiscoPoP saw before?

## Result in one paragraph

Running (10 Oct). On the Mac: 9 of 9 packages validated; on s341 the form that computes the positions once reproduces the output on the data of every earlier run and changes it on the new data.

## Change-log rows that name these runs (§6)

| Date | Repo | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-10 | plan | **Packaging v8 (suite `tsvc_c4`): the loops of the contrast set and `s341` on data that move — what is in it and by which rule, what was proven on the Mac, and the no-model checks on the server (T0.19) with their criteria. Written before the packages enter the repository and before anything runs on the server; no model reads a package before the author has seen its file.** **The rule for the loops** (fixed here, before any trial and before DiscoPoP has been run on any of them): every loop of TSVC's sections "reductions" and "search loops" that is not in the main set already (`s313`, `s3112`, `s331` are) and can be packaged so that every repetition is necessary and the result is finite at the measurement size. DiscoPoP alone, in three draws without a model, then splits them: a loop it parallelizes itself is a CONTROL, a loop it leaves unchanged is in the SET UNDER TEST. **What the rule leaves out, with the reason** — the author had been named eight loops on 10 Oct (`s314`, `s315`, `s316`, `s318`, `s3110`, `s13110`, `s3113`, `s332`), named from their headings before they were read: `s13110` — its text is `s3110`'s, statement for statement (`tsvc.c`): one loop, not two. `s3110` — it searches the two-dimensional `aa`, which the packaging's `dummy` does not change between repetitions, so no repetition is necessary (the hole v7 closed), and TSVC's 256 × 256 elements are far below a measurable size. `s332` — the first element above a threshold: the sequential loop stops at its first match, and the elements `dummy` changes sit at the start of the array at the measurement size (`(n·7919 + 13) mod LEN_1D`, n < 48, against 192,000,000 elements), so a result that moves between repetitions puts the match there and leaves nothing to search; in TSVC itself the threshold is a real read through an `int` pointer (`time_function(&s332, &s1)`). `s31111` — no loop over the data inside a repetition (eight calls on four elements each). `s312`, `s317` — a product over the whole length is zero or infinite at the measurement size. **What the rule adds that he was not named:** the three sums `s311`, `s3111`, `s319` — the expected control: the same shape of loop with an operator DiscoPoP's reduction clause covers (it writes `+ − * & \| ^`, `profiler/DiscoPoP/dp_reduction/utils.cpp`). **Packaged, eight new loops:** `s311`, `s3111`, `s319` (expected control); `s314` (largest value), `s316` (smallest value), `s3113` (largest absolute value) — the reference is TSVC's loop with one clause, `reduction(max:…)` or `reduction(min:…)`; `s315` (largest value and the first index holding it), `s318` (the same on absolute values at a stride) — no clause exists for the pair; the reference keeps a pair per thread and merges them under a lock. Five loops expected under test, not eight; said to the author with the files. **Packaging v8 is v7** (the repetition loop inside the function, `dummy` recording every repetition and handed the number the repetition computed) **with:** (a) *data in which each new loop's result moves between repetitions*, as v7 gave `s331`: `dummy` adds 0.25 to one element of `a` per call at positions the measurement header knows; a ladder of values on those positions spanning less than 0.25 makes the element just raised the new largest (`s314`, `s315`, `s318`, `s3113`: 2.0 + 0.005·n) or makes the smallest element the one raised next (`s316`: −2.0 + 0.005·n); `a[0]`, which `dummy` raises by 0.125 per call, overtakes the ladder after about a quarter of the repetitions and is the largest from then on — a new value in every repetition on either input. `s3111` gets negative elements so that its test decides something. The sums move by themselves. (b) *`s341` on other data:* the elements of `b` that `dummy` raises start at −0.1, so one more element is positive in every repetition and every later position of the packed array shifts. (c) *a third variant the generator proves wrong for `s341`* (`hoist`): the form of every program that won this loop in E1-v6 and E3 with its directive removed — the positions computed once, in front of the repetitions. (d) three details of the files a model reads: `ABS`, which TSVC defines as `fabs` in `common.h`, is defined in `data.h` with `#include <math.h>` (`s318`, `s3113`); `s318`'s stride `inc` is a hidden value as `s171`'s (TSVC's driver passes 1); and from `s315` the two lines with which TSVC's own function fills `a` in front of the repetitions are removed — data set-up, which is the measurement header's here (with them the function would overwrite the header's data and the perturbed input). The generator's change is confined to a new suite: `tsvc_c2` and `tsvc_c3` regenerate byte for byte after it (compared with the baseline taken at `0c7723749`). **Proven on the Mac, in a scratch folder** (`prepare_tsvc.py --layout v8 --suite tsvc_c4 --validate`): 9 of 9 packages validated — output finite, changed by the perturbed input, deterministic; the reference equal to the original on both inputs at 4 threads; the variants `skip` and `reorder` change the output on both inputs for every package; `hoist` changes `s341`'s output on both inputs (largest relative difference 0.885 and 0.906). The same variant on v7's `s341` (`tsvc_c3`, the data of every run so far) reproduces the output exactly on both inputs — the hole, shown without a model. **T0.19 — the server checks, no model; criteria fixed here.** (1) *Packages:* built with the generator's validation on the server; 9 validated, none failed; every file of every package and every measurement header with the same sha256 as on the Mac. (2) *Sizes* (`t0_1_c4_sizes`, `size_table.py`, NUMA node 0, nothing else running; merged into `config/kernel_sizes.json`): each package gets its timing and verification size as every one-vector loop does; `s341` is expected at the sizes of its `tsvc_c2` package. A loop that does not reach a measurable time at the largest size cannot be judged for speed and leaves the set — reported. (3) *Classes* (`t0_11_c4_a`, `_b`, `_c`: arm `discopop_capability`, threads 6 and 12, 5 timing repeats, one trial per package, three 12-core groups at once): the rule's split. Expected: `s311`, `s3111`, `s319` parallelized by DiscoPoP alone (control); `s314`, `s316`, `s3113`, `s315`, `s318` unchanged (under test); `s341` unchanged, as on `tsvc_c2`. The measured class decides, not the expectation; a loop whose three draws disagree is put to the author. (4) *References* (`t0_14_c4_refs`: the nine references as the benchmark's file through `verify-source`, threads 6 and 12, 5 repeats): each verified correct on both inputs; its speed-up reported. A loop under test whose reference is not FASTER leaves the set — there is nothing to win on it. (5) *The ceiling of the setup in which DiscoPoP writes* (`t0_13_c4_ceiling`: `default_arm_ceiling.py`, the reference of each loop under test with its directives removed, no model): does DiscoPoP write a directive on it? Expected: on none of the five. It says what that setup can win with the reference's own form; it does not say no other rewrite exists that DiscoPoP can annotate — that is what the trials are for. (6) *`s341`, DiscoPoP's view on the new data against v7's* (`t0_19_s341_a`, `_b`: `layout_equivalence.py --old tsvc_c3 --new tsvc_c4 --added-values 2`, the one package, two draws): the output differs by design; the agent's candidates, the Do-All set, the blocker of the loop, the repetition loop's verdict and the order statement must not differ in both draws. **After T0.19:** the classes into `config/benchmark_classes.json`; the eight new files shown to the author; the contrast set's experiment and `s341`'s re-run pre-registered with their cost; nothing with a model before his OK. | Plan, packaging v8 and T0.19 |
